title: The moments, and what answers them
description: Every operational moment this tool is a response to, with who recognises it, the operational area it falls under, and the commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases that answer it. A moment that named something this repository does not have would fail validation rather than draw an edge to nothing.
source: the front matter of every object of kind `moment`

node_kinds.area: the operational area it falls under
node_kinds.capability: a capability of this executable that answers it
node_kinds.claim: a claim that says what is guaranteed here
node_kinds.rule: a rule of the effective set that governs it
node_kinds.use-case: a use case that shows the way out

edge_kinds.answered_by: that command or capability answers this moment
edge_kinds.backed_by: that claim says what is guaranteed here
edge_kinds.falls_under: this moment falls under that area
edge_kinds.related_to: the moment names that one as related
edge_kinds.resolved_by: that use case shows the way out

nodes.label: Contract drift
nodes.summary: A contract maintained by hand beside the code it describes goes stale on the first change that forgets it.

nodes.label: Unverified done
nodes.summary: A fluent completion claim is accepted as evidence because nothing wrote down, beforehand, what would have to be true.

nodes.label: Settled, then reopened
nodes.summary: A decision whose reason lived in a conversation cannot be reviewed, only re-argued — by a worker with less information than the first one had.

nodes.label: Re-explaining context
nodes.summary: Repository knowledge that only ever existed in a conversation has to be re-transmitted by hand to every worker that follows.

nodes.label: Maximum effort by default
nodes.summary: Capability, reasoning depth, context size and verbosity collapse into one habit — everything on — because nothing ever named them separately.

nodes.label: Three roadmaps
nodes.summary: A plan kept in prose is a snapshot, and every copy of it drifts on its own schedule; stored status is an assertion that stays true after the world moves.

nodes.label: Duplicated work
nodes.summary: Two workers spend a day each on one defect because ownership was implicit and neither could see the other.

nodes.label: Two rulebooks
nodes.summary: Each provider reads its own hand-edited file, nothing relates them, and which contract applies depends on which tool is open.

nodes.label: Only transcripts
nodes.summary: A conversation log records what was said, not what happened, so the operational question has to be answered by a person reading prose.
